questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following curve represents the first order reaction ?
options: (A) $t_{1/2}$ vs $[R]_0$ showing a straight line with positive slope starting from origin
(B) $t_{1/2}$ vs $[R]_0$ showing a horizontal straight line parallel to $[R]_0$ axis
(C) Rate vs Concentration showing a horizontal straight line parallel to Concentration axis
(D) Rate vs Concentration showing a hyperbolically decreasing curve
questions.solution: For a first order reaction, half-life $t_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{k}$, which is independent of the initial concentration $[R]_0$. Therefore, a plot of $t_{1/2}$ versus $[R]_0$ is a horizontal straight line parallel to the concentration axis.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following solutions will have the lowest freezing point in water ?
questions.solution: Depression in freezing point $\Delta T_f = i \cdot K_f \cdot m$. A higher value of the van 't Hoff factor ($i$) gives a greater depression in freezing point, resulting in a lower freezing point. For $\text{CaCl}_2$, $i = 3$, which is highest among the given options.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following is not a transition metal ?
questions.solution: Mercury (Hg) has a completely filled d-orbital ($d^{10}$) in its ground state as well as in its common oxidation states, so it is not considered a transition element.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following represents the fraction of molecules with energies equal to or greater than $E_a$ ?
questions.solution: According to the Arrhenius equation, the Boltzmann factor $e^{-E_a/RT}$ represents the fraction of molecules having energy equal to or greater than the activation energy $E_a$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What will happen during the electrolysis of aqueous solution of $\text{CuCl}_2$ by using platinum electrodes ?
options: $\text{H}_2$ gas will be released at cathode
$\text{O}_2$ gas will be released at anode
$\text{Cl}_2$ gas will be released at anode
questions.solution: At the cathode, $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ is reduced to $\text{Cu}(s)$. At the anode, oxidation of $\text{Cl}^-$ ions occurs preferentially over water due to the overpotential of oxygen, releasing $\text{Cl}_2$ gas at the anode.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Aspirin is obtained by acetylation of
questions.solution: Acetylation of 2-hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid) with acetic anhydride in the presence of an acid catalyst yields acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The secondary valency of Co in the complex $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5(\text{NO}_2)]^{2+}$ is
questions.solution: Secondary valency corresponds to the coordination number of the central metal ion. Co is bonded to 5 monodentate $\text{NH}_3$ ligands and 1 monodentate $\text{NO}_2^-$ ligand, giving a total coordination number (secondary valency) of 6.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: At low temperature, phenol reacts with dil. $\text{HNO}_3$ to yield
questions.solution: Phenol reacts with dilute nitric acid at low temperature (298 K) to give a mixture of ortho-nitrophenol and para-nitrophenol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following is ‘not’ true about enantiomers ?
options: They have the same chemical reactivity.
They have the same specific rotation.
They have the same melting or boiling point.
They have the same refractive index.
questions.solution: Enantiomers rotate the plane of polarized light by equal amounts but in opposite directions. Thus, they have specific rotations of equal magnitude but opposite signs, not identical specific rotation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution: Direct nitration of aniline in strongly acidic medium leads to the formation of anilinium ion which is meta-directing, giving a product mixture of 51% para, 47% meta, and 2% ortho derivatives.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following amines has lowest $\text{pK}_b$ value ?
questions.solution: Lowest $\text{pK}_b$ value corresponds to the strongest base. In $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5 - \text{N}(\text{CH}_3)_2$, two electron-releasing methyl groups increase electron density on the nitrogen atom, making it the most basic among the given options.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The deficiency of which of the following vitamins causes increased fragility of red blood cells and muscular weakness :
questions.solution: Deficiency of Vitamin E leads to increased fragility of red blood cells (hemolytic anemia) and muscular weakness.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A) : It is not possible to separate the components of an azeotrope by fractional distillation.
Reason (R) : Components of an azeotrope have the same composition in liquid and vapour phase and boil at a constant temperature.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Azeotropes boil at a constant temperature with identical composition in both liquid and vapour phases, making separation of their components by fractional distillation impossible. Thus, both A and R are true and R correctly explains A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A) : The presence of –OH group in phenols directs the incoming group to meta position in the ring.
Reason (R) : –OH group in phenols activates the aromatic ring towards electrophilic substitution reaction.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: The –OH group in phenol is ortho- and para-directing due to resonance activation, making Assertion (A) false. The –OH group activates the ring towards electrophilic substitution, making Reason (R) true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A) : Actinoids show wide range of oxidation states.
Reason (R) : Actinoids are radioactive in nature.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Actinoids show a wide range of oxidation states because 5f, 6d, and 7s levels are of comparable energies. While actinoids are radioactive in nature, radioactivity is not the explanation for their multiple oxidation states.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A) : The pentaacetate of glucose does not react with $\text{H}_2\text{N} - \text{OH}$.
Reason (R) : It indicates the presence of free – CHO group in glucose.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Glucose pentaacetate does not react with hydroxylamine because it locks the cyclic hemiacetal structure and lacks a free –CHO group. Thus, Reason (R) stating that it indicates the presence of a free –CHO group is false.
